issue: h₂énǵʰos 'narrowness' for 'sorrow' is the Lat. angor sense, acceptable; relative h₁yéh₂ agrees with the goddess.
2pl gʷm̥té/h₃slidʰté to the herd, mē-kʷe kʷis n̥ḱyéh₁t 'let no one be lost', lewkós agrees with masc. h₂éydʰos; sédesi 'in the dwelling' per lexicon gloss.
dyubʰós is dat./abl. PLURAL of dyḗws ('to the skies/gods') where the English has 'Give Dyeus a gift' (dat. sg. diwéy). Also mē moy kʷim déh₃s uses animate kʷím 'anyone' for 'nothing' (neuter kʷíd).
Dual eyes h₃ókʷih₁ take 3du optative widóyh₁tām; mē + injunctive prohibitive; correlative h₁yós … só.
Tier 1 (Lühr-type) notation: h₂wlh₂néh₂, unmarked syllabic m (wéǵʰontm, méǵoh₂m), parenthesised (H)/(h₁), full-grade gʷérh₂um; faithful to source but clashes with corpus conventions.
First-person dying warrior; ḱéyh₂er 1sg middle, gʷr̥h₃ṓnti subj. 3pl, mē HréwdHs prohibitive, h₁éseti future-subjunctive 'shall be'.
h₁yós gʰóstis dʰrugʰyéti: gʰóstis is NOMINATIVE, so the PIE says 'the guest who deceives', not 'whoever deceives the guest'; needs acc. gʰóstim (which the last sentence has).

Reflexive swéh₂ 'his own' (with h₃ésth₁h₂) refers to the man, not to the subject (water, addressed); a non-reflexive h₁ésyo would be regular. Final gʷíh₃weti has a distant null subject (the man), readable.

Ambiguous antecedent: h₁yód wĺ̥kʷos h₁ért h₁ím úd ǵʰéyt — the subordinate subject is the wolf and the main clause has a null subject, so PIE most naturally reads 'the wolf drove him out'; English means the dog drove the wolf out. Needs an explicit subject.
Tier 1 Schleicher-style transcription (no laryngeals, a-vocalism, warnā, akwams); faithful to source, clashes with corpus notation.
Plural horses with ḱéyro / stesth₂ḗr / sth₂ént / gʷh₂ént and h₁íns; 2pl imperatives to the horses. péh₂wr̥-kʷe dʰégʷʰet is transitive-or-intransitive ambiguous, matches 'fire burned'.
Vocatives dyéw ph₂ter, dʰéǵʰom méh₂ter; fem. h₁íh₂m̥ for grain; sph₁réh₂es agrees with fem. h₂óweyes; mē + middle optative Hrumpih₁tó.
gʰósteyes 'guests/strangers' rendered 'enemies' (the Latin hostis development, a stretched sense for PIE); bʰoréyont iterative 'carried around' for 'carried off'.
péruti h₂uksté: h₂uksté is 2PL aorist, but the addressee is the single brother ('you grew tall'); needs 2sg h₂wéks.
gʷā́m writes the Stang outcome of the 1sg root aorist (same notation point as t021/t023/t030). Otherwise fine: fem. h₁íh₂m̥ for the root, h₁ím for the guest.
Participle vocative sérpont with h₂éngʷʰey; mē + injunctive prohibitives; kʷéḱt aorist for 'sees' (accepted convention).
h₁íh₂m̥ for the sister, mē h₁éps prohibitive. Null subject of widét after nókʷts léytt is understood from context (the brother).
Formulaic ḱléwos ń̥dʰgʷʰitom; fem. méǵh₂ih₂ with wéyHs; 3pl stesth₂ḗr HrudHénti.
Negated aorists; n̥smé mē linékʷs; enclitic nos as dative of disadvantage.
Neuter plural h₂éḱruh₂ with singular verb (archaic rule); desiderative wéydsoh₂; h₁opéyēti 'bring to'.
Repetition charm; fem. h₁íh₂m̥ for the wool. Final h₁ésmi (m./n. loc.) is best read as 'in it (the honey, neuter)'; English 'in it' is equally open.
bʰéh₂os sn̥gʷtā́m: sn̥gʷtā́m is 3DU aorist with a singular subject ('the light goes down'); needs 3sg séngʷt (used in the next sentence).
pérkʷunos pérkʷum stunddʰí: the addressee of the 2sg imperative is in the NOMINATIVE; needs vocative pérkʷune (as in 53d24214 and 757f618e).
h₁ím / h₁íd / h₁íh₂m̥ correctly track horse, bone (n.) and grain (f.); h₁ésmey is the horse (subject is the man).
Blood-stopping charm; h₁íd (n.) for the sore/blood, both neuter; middle aorist Hwr̥tó 'is shut'; trís wéwkom.
ḱéyor 3sg middle, rhetorical kʷís questions with subjunctives, mr̥tṓs-ge.
Tier 1 fable line in an older, laryngeal-less notation (ḱeḱruwos, owis, aǵrom, ebʰuget with augment); faithful to source, clashes with corpus notation.
Indefinite kʷesyo, neuter h₁íd for the arm (dóws n.), mē + injunctive sth₂éh₁yet, h₁yós wóyde 'the one who knows'.
